title: Buying a licence and knowing what it unlocks
target: What a licence actually is in Supermarket Simulator — an item with a tab, a record on each product and a difference between unlocked and active — so a purchase is understood rather than guessed at.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: The computer or tablet in reach
A product line you want to sell

steps.do: Treat a licence as an item you buy rather than as a switch you flip.
steps.because: a licence is bought as an item, listed in a tab of its own with an indicator for a purchase (LicenseItem, LicensesTab, PurchasedLicenseIndicator)

steps.do: Read the licence tab as a screen with its own layout.
steps.because: the licence tab has a layout configuration of its own (LicenseLayoutConfig)

steps.do: Know that the connection runs the other way as well: the product carries the licence, and separately the game describes what a licence unlocks.
steps.because: a product carries a licence record and there is separate data describing what a licence unlocks (ProductLicenseSO, LicenseProductsData, productLicenseSos)

steps.do: Keep unlocked and active licences apart in your head.
steps.because: unlocked licences and active licences are kept apart, and a set of licence numbers can be disabled (unlockedLicenses, activeLicenses, disabledLicenseIDs)

steps.do: Expect the purchase to be checked rather than simply charged.
steps.because: buying a licence is checked, with a store-side handle and a result, and there are add-on licences (storeCanAcquireLicenseResult, storeLicenseHandle, addOnLicenses)

steps.do: Use the icons to scan a long licence list.
steps.because: licence icons are kept on sheets grouped by kind and by range of licence numbers (asset names: T_IconAtlasLicence-1-10, T_IconAtlasLicence-Vegetables, T_IconAtlasLicense-11-20)

commonMistakes: Assuming a bought licence is an active one.
Looking for a product's licence on the shelf rather than on the product record.
Ignoring add-on licences because the main purchase looked complete.
Hunting through a long list by name when the icons are grouped by kind and number.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
